blocks.text: Most of the plan runs on budgets that already exist; the capital it needs sits with ACSA, PRASA, Transnet and private investors, and none of it has been costed yet.

No deliverable costs any initiative. The Inception Report scoped an investment opportunity framework with return scoring, but no separate output was delivered (Inception Report, Nov 2025, p18, p20), and stakeholders describe Western Cape tourism funding as materially below peer destinations without giving a figure (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p25). Thirteen initiatives draw mainly on Wesgro's operating budget, and four need private capital as a main source; the initiatives table in section 4.1 gives each one's main and supporting funding routes. This section leaves the rand bands to be set with Wesgro Finance and DEDAT [cost band per initiative and phase: Wesgro Finance and DEDAT to set before Steerco signs off the plan]. Wesgro Finance and DEDAT also agree a stop list before Gate 1, naming the Wesgro work deprioritised to fund the initiatives (section 4.8). [Open item: Wesgro Finance to give an indicative rand band for the first 24 months.]

callout.text: Wesgro's operating budget is the main source for 13 initiatives, and private capital for the four capital-heavy ones.

blocks.text: **Crowding in capital.** The rule for capital is the Inclusion Plan's: invest after demand is shown, and attach a maintenance and marketing covenant to any public asset (SME and Community Inclusion Plan, Sep 2026, p15, p31, p32). Wesgro's investment promotion work builds the tourism pipeline from the Infrastructure Report's gap-closure tables, where every district lists tourism gaps with no committed capital (I14; Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p32 to p87). The air access fund scales Cape Town Air Access's existing route fund with public and private money (I6).

**What the SLA asks and what is still to do.** The SLA asks for return projections on infrastructure priorities (clause 1.1.8.3) [clause wording to be checked against the signed Annexure B]. Those need costed projects, and the only costed items in hand are the airport, rail and port programmes the province does not fund. The return case is therefore an output of I14 in Phase 1, built project by project as the pipeline forms.
